A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, appendices, and supplementary plots. Retained content can be matched across the reorganization and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original filter-training experiments, hidden-state measurements, and attention-head ablations in Sections 3–4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds DH amplification, threshold-sensitivity experiments, additional model evaluations, and translation experiments.

M1.justification: The low-rank filter, TVS metrics, and denoising-head identification procedure are retained. Section 4.4 adds an inference intervention that multiplies identified DH outputs by (1 + lambda). The three-step framework otherwise reorganizes existing procedures.

E1.justification: The six classification datasets and two fact-recall datasets are retained. Appendix H adds OPUS-100 English-to-Chinese translation, substantially extending coverage to bilingual, multi-token generation, although the authors describe this investigation as prototypical.

E2.justification: The comparisons retain zero-shot or unmodified ICL and ablation of equal numbers of randomly selected heads per layer. Added checkpoints are evaluation backbones using these existing controls; no distinct competing algorithm is introduced or removed.

E3.justification: v2 adds Qwen 2.5-3B Instruct evaluations, SST-2-only DH ablation for Llama 3-13B Instruct, and amplification/threshold sweeps. Existing filter-training budgets, test sizes, and decoding procedures remain unchanged. Table 2 also corrects v1's blanket 50% layer-coverage statement to explicit counts, including 7/32 for Llama 3-8B; retained scores do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: Figure 14 newly tests whether DH amplification improves accuracy under true and random labels. Appendix E tests sensitivity to the DH-selection threshold against random-head ablation. Appendix H examines information-removal dynamics on translation and retained fact-recall tasks, while supplementary DH diagnostics extend to Qwen Instruct. These substantially expand the mechanism and robustness analyses.

E5.justification: Table 2 adds probabilities labeled P-values, defined through comparison with the lower tail of random-head ablation accuracy. v1 has no corresponding significance column. No new seed or repeated-run counts are disclosed, and the calculation procedure remains underspecified; additional runs cannot be inferred.

E6.justification: v2 adds amplification, threshold-sensitivity, translation, and instruction-tuned-model results. For example, new Table 2 entries report Qwen 2.5-3B Instruct unseen-label accuracy of 48.70% unablated and 37.51% with DH ablation. Original Table 2 scores remain unchanged. Table 6 also changes Qwen 2.5-7B's average 8-shot accuracy from 74.41% to 77.25% despite unchanged dataset rows, introducing an internal inconsistency rather than demonstrating a performance gain.

T1.justification: v1 provides a covariance-flux definition and informal entropy motivation. New Appendix G introduces Hausdorff differential entropy for possibly rank-deficient Gaussian distributions, Theorem 1 relating entropy to nonzero covariance eigenvalues, and a proof in Equations 2–10. This is substantial new formal content, although Equation 7 contains signs inconsistent with Equations 6 and 9.

C1.justification: v2's introduction adds a generally applicable information-removal evaluation framework as its first contribution, extending the stated methodological scope beyond ICL. The abstract and central claims about information removal, denoising heads, and unseen-label behavior remain essentially unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 5 adds the limitation that linear filters assume linearly separable features and may require nonlinear replacements for manifold representations. Appendix H interprets translation dynamics as removing non-target-language verbalizations while acknowledging the absence of covariance-flux verification and DH localization there. Earlier mechanism interpretations and bijective-task limitations are retained.

D1.justification: v2 supplies a title-page code-repository link, the Qwen Instruct checkpoint, and an OPUS-100 prompt template. It explicitly documents eight-shot DH experiments, scanned-layer counts, and the ±2.5% threshold used in Qwen head-count plots. Existing optimizer, training-budget, and test-set details are retained; the linked code's availability was not independently verified.

R1.justification: v2 adds Modell et al. (2025) for representation manifolds and Zhang et al. (2020) and Tiedemann (2012) for translation data. The positioning relative to induction heads, task vectors, and in-weight learning remains largely unchanged.

P1.justification: v1 interleaves methods and findings across Sections 3–4. v2 creates a standalone three-step Method section and reorganizes experiments into corresponding Steps 1–3 in Section 4, with rewritten contribution statements and transitions. The appendix structure also expands and reorganizes from A–F to A–I.

P2.justification: v2 adds amplification, threshold, translation, and Qwen Instruct figure series, expands Tables 2, 6, and 7, and adds P-values and layer-coverage information to Table 2. Numerous retained figures move, and conceptual diagrams are refined. Figures 42–46 provide dedicated covariance-out-of-rank curves, largely redisplaying quantities previously represented by marker size.

improvement.justification: The amplification intervention and threshold-sensitivity study strengthen causal and robustness evidence missing from v1, while the reorganized method and explicit nonlinear limitations improve clarity. These support a limited net gain. However, v2 introduces incorrect Qwen averages in Table 6 and a sign inconsistency in its entropy proof. Its new Qwen Instruct results also retain substantial unseen-label accuracy after ablation, fitting the unchanged near-zero claims poorly. These reporting and interpretation weaknesses limit the improvement.
